recommendedTextbook.title: Essential Government for Senior Secondary Schools
recommendedTextbook.author: C. C. Dibie
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: The 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
subtopics: Origins and promulgation of the 1999 Constitution under Decree No. 24
Features: Presidential democracy, 36 states, separation of powers, exclusive and concurrent legislative lists
Constitutional amendment procedures and ongoing restructuring debates
objectives: Analyze key structural features of the 1999 Constitution
Differentiate exclusive, concurrent, and residual legislative lists
Evaluate arguments for state police and fiscal federalism in Nigeria

topics.topic: Military Rule in Nigerian Political History
subtopics: First military coup of January 15, 1966, counter-coup of July 1966, and civil war (1967-1970)
Causes of military intervention in Nigerian politics (election rigging, corruption, ethnic rivalry)
Structure of military governments (SMC/AFRC/PRC) and decrees vs rule of law
objectives: Identify 5 internal socio-political causes of military coups d'état
Evaluate positive and negative impacts of military rule on Nigerian development
Explain mechanisms employed by military regimes to repress democratic dissent

topics.topic: Nigeria's Foreign Policy and Afrocentric Diplomacy
subtopics: Basic principles of Nigerian foreign policy (Africa as centerpiece, non-alignment, sovereign equality)
Nigeria's role in the liberation of Southern Africa and anti-apartheid campaigns
Establishment and peace-keeping leadership in ECOWAS and ECOMOG
objectives: Define foreign policy and explain Nigeria's Afrocentric foreign doctrine
Evaluate Nigeria's leadership in the formation of ECOWAS and mediation in Liberia/Sierra Leone
Analyze contemporary economic diplomacy and bilateral relations with world powers

topics.topic: International Organizations: AU, ECOWAS, Commonwealth and UN
subtopics: African Union (AU): Transformation from OAU, organs, and African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)
Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS): Free movement of persons and trade protocols
The United Nations (UN): Security Council, General Assembly, and Nigeria's peacekeeping contributions
objectives: Compare the charter of the OAU with the modern AU Constitutive Act
Evaluate the achievements and obstacles of ECOWAS trade integration
Assess Nigeria's quest for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council
